taxonomy.note: Accepted spelling is Salvia pentstemonoides (extra t). U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service explicitly notes that penstemonoides is a common misspelling. Preserve the Master Plant Pool source spelling for provenance but use pentstemonoides for the canonical taxon.

evidence: Bandera — NPSOT historical/rediscovery account documents wild populations in Bandera County.
Real — NPSOT account explicitly documents a private-land wild population in Real County.
Kerr — NPSOT reports rediscovery of a large wild population along the Guadalupe River in Kerr County; historical Kerr specimens are also noted.
Gillespie — U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service identifies the 1845 upper Pedernales type material from Gillespie County as historical backup evidence.
target_zone_range.guardrail: No county presence inferred from source-pool membership or cultivated records.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with the basal rosette and habitat: a large perennial rosette in intermittently moist limestone canyon/seep habitat sends up tall flowering stalks with unusually large red to rose-red flowers.
diagnostic_traits: perennial herb with persistent basal rosette

confusers.separator: Both can be red, but Big Red Sage has a much larger basal rosette, taller flowering stalk, much larger flowers, and a moist limestone-seep/canyon niche.

installation_guardrail: Do not install until Calvin explicitly approves.
